s1.syndrome_frame: Painless vulvar mass with gradual enlargement
salient_findings: Painless right vulvar mass extending into the right inguinal region
Mass measured 12 cm and was non-tender
Soft-tissue ultrasound showed a well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass
key_facts: 67-year-old woman
Noted the lesion two years earlier
Gradual enlargement over the past four months
Denied pain, changes in appetite or bowel habits, urinary symptoms, weight loss, infection, or bleeding
Medical history notable for hypertension and hysterectomy in 2016
Post-menopausal with no history of hormone therapy
Does not smoke or drink alcohol
Afebrile with normal vital signs
Abdominal exam was unremarkable
Pelvic exam was otherwise normal
Soft-tissue ultrasound showed a well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass
Routine laboratory results were within normal limits

differentials: Hydrocele of the canal of Nuck
Giant cell tumor of the soft tissue
Smooth muscle tumor of uncertain malignant potential

Giant cell tumor of the soft tissue
Smooth muscle tumor of uncertain malignant potential

shortlist.label: Canal of Nuck hernia
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the leading preoperative impression and ultrasound findings

shortlist.label: Vulvar lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common benign tumor that could present as a painless vulvar mass

shortlist.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare but plausible diagnosis given the gradual enlargement and ultrasound characteristics

shortlist.label: Vulvar leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign tumor that could present as a painless vulvar mass, although less common than lipoma

shortlist.label: Bartholin gland carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, it is a rare but important diagnosis to consider given the patient's age and presentation

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a painless right vulvar mass extending into the right inguinal region, along with the ultrasound findings of a well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass tracking into the inguinal canal, is consistent with a Canal of Nuck hernia, especially given the preoperative impression and the absence of symptoms suggestive of malignancy or infection.

rejected.label: Vulvar lipoma
rejected.why: While possible, the mass's extension into the inguinal canal and the ultrasound characteristics are more suggestive of a hernia than a lipoma.

rejected.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a slow-growing, painless mass, but it is less likely given the ultrasound findings and the lack of other characteristic features such as fixation to surrounding tissues.

rejected.label: Vulvar leiomyoma
rejected.why: Leiomyomas are rare in the vulva and the described mass's characteristics and location are not typical for this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Bartholin gland carcinoma
rejected.why: The absence of symptoms such as pain, bleeding, or signs of infection, along with the ultrasound findings, makes this malignant diagnosis less likely.
